ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
As shown in the figure, an inclined plane with an angle $\theta{=}37^{\circ}$ and height $h{=}1.8\mathrm{m}$ is located on a horizontal ground. A small ball is thrown horizontally to the right from point A at the top of the inclined plane with an initial velocity $v_{0}$, and the ball just lands at point B at the bottom of the inclined plane. Air resistance is negligible, and the gravitational acceleration is taken as $g{=}10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, with $\tan 37^{\circ}=0.75$.

1. Determine the magnitude of the initial velocity $v_{0}$ of the projectile.
2. If the inclined plane starts to move to the right with a uniformly accelerated linear motion from rest on the horizontal plane at the same time the ball is thrown horizontally, and the ball lands on the inclined plane after $t_{2}=0.3\mathrm{s}$, find the magnitude of the acceleration of the inclined plane.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, point A is at the upper-left end of the inclined plane, directly below A is the left-end foot point on the horizontal ground, and the vertical height is labeled h. The small ball is thrown horizontally to the right from point A, and the initial velocity is labeled v0. The inclined plane extends from A downward to the right to point B on the ground, the angle between inclined plane AB and the horizontal ground is labeled 37°, and B is on the ground on the right side. Reasoning: Take the fixed ground reference frame, set the ground point directly below A as the coordinate origin, the x-axis horizontal to the right, and the y-axis vertical upward, then the coordinate of point A is (0,h), and the coordinate of point B is (L,0). From the right-triangle relationship in the figure, the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal is 37°, so tan37° = h/L, therefore L = h/tan37° = 1.8/0.75 = 2.4 m. First question: The small ball is thrown horizontally from point A, and the equations of motion are x = v0 t, y = h - (1/2)gt^2. When the small ball just lands at point B, y=0, so 0 = 1.8 - (1/2)×10×t^2, giving t = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(3.6/10) = 0.6 s. At this time x=L=2.4 m, so v0 = L/t = 2.4/0.6 = 4 m/s. Second question: The inclined plane starts from rest and makes uniformly accelerated linear motion to the right; when t2=0.3 s, the horizontal displacement is s = (1/2)at2^2. After the whole inclined plane moves to the right, its line equation is y = h - tan37°(x - s). The small ball still makes horizontal projectile motion in the ground reference frame; when t2=0.3 s, x = v0 t2 = 4×0.3 = 1.2 m, y = h - (1/2)gt2^2 = 1.8 - 0.5×10×0.3^2 = 1.35 m. Substitute into the moved inclined-plane equation: 1.35 = 1.8 - 0.75(1.2 - s). Simplifying gives 1.35 = 0.9 + 0.75s, so s = 0.6 m. Also s = (1/2)a×0.3^2, therefore a = 2s/t2^2 = 1.2/0.09 = 13.3 m/s^2.

raw_record.question_text:
As shown in the figure, an inclined plane with an angle $\theta=37^{\circ}$ and height $h=1.8\mathrm{m}$ is located on a horizontal ground. A small ball is thrown horizontally to the right from point A at the top of the inclined plane with an initial velocity $v_{0}$, and the ball just lands at point B at the bottom of the inclined plane. Air resistance is negligible, and the gravitational acceleration is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, with $\tan 37^{\circ}=0.75$.

1. Determine the magnitude of the initial velocity $v_{0}$ of the projectile.
2. If the inclined plane starts to move to the right with a uniformly accelerated linear motion from rest on the horizontal plane at the same time the ball is thrown horizontally, and the ball lands on the inclined plane after $t_{2}=0.3\mathrm{s}$, find the magnitude of the acceleration of the inclined plane.

method.method_draft: Use a fixed ground-frame Cartesian coordinate setup. From the image, take A as vertically above the left foot of the incline, B on the ground to the right, and the incline AB making 37 degrees with the horizontal. Let the horizontal distance from the foot below A to B be L. The visual triangle gives L = h / tan37. For part 1, write projectile motion from A: x = v0 t, y = h - (1/2)gt^2. At B, y = 0 and x = L, so t = sqrt(2h/g), then v0 = L/t. For part 2, the whole incline translates right by s = (1/2)at2^2. Its line at time t2 is y = h - tan37 * (x - s). The ball is at x = v0 t2, y = h - (1/2)g t2^2. Substitute these into the moving line equation and solve for a.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：附图中，点A在斜面左上端，A的正下方是水平地面上的左端脚点，竖直高度标为h。小球从A点水平向右抛出，初速度标为v0。斜面从A向右下方延伸到地面上的点B，斜面AB与水平地面夹角标为37°，B在右侧地面上。

推理：取固定地面参考系，设A正下方的地面点为坐标原点，x轴水平向右，y轴竖直向上，则A点坐标为(0,h)，B点坐标为(L,0)。由图中直角三角形关系，斜面与水平夹角为37°，所以 tan37° = h/L，因此 L = h/tan37° = 1.8/0.75 = 2.4 m。

第一问：小球从A点水平抛出，运动方程为 x = v0 t，y = h - (1/2)gt^2。小球刚好落到B点时 y=0，所以 0 = 1.8 - (1/2)×10×t^2，得 t = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(3.6/10) = 0.6 s。此时 x=L=2.4 m，所以 v0 = L/t = 2.4/0.6 = 4 m/s。

第二问：斜面从静止开始向右做匀加速直线运动，t2=0.3 s时水平位移为 s = (1/2)at2^2。斜面整体右移后，其直线方程为 y = h - tan37°(x - s)。小球仍在地面参考系中做平抛运动，t2=0.3 s时 x = v0 t2 = 4×0.3 = 1.2 m，y = h - (1/2)gt2^2 = 1.8 - 0.5×10×0.3^2 = 1.35 m。代入移动后斜面方程：1.35 = 1.8 - 0.75(1.2 - s)。化简得 1.35 = 0.9 + 0.75s，所以 s = 0.6 m。又 s = (1/2)a×0.3^2，因此 a = 2s/t2^2 = 1.2/0.09 = 13.3 m/s^2。

method.method_draft: Use geometric displacement ratios rather than writing the incline as a full line equation. From the image, the slope means any point on the incline has vertical drop divided by horizontal run equal to tan37. For part 1, the ball must drop the full height h, so vertical motion gives h = (1/2)gt1^2. The needed horizontal run to B is h/tan37, so v0 = (h/tan37)/t1. For part 2, after t2 = 0.3 s the ball has vertically dropped Δy = (1/2)gt2^2. Therefore, relative to the moving incline’s top, the horizontal distance corresponding to that drop along the slope must be Δx_rel = Δy/tan37. The ball’s ground-frame horizontal displacement is v0 t2, so the incline’s rightward displacement must be s = v0 t2 - Δx_rel. Since the incline starts from rest with constant acceleration, s = (1/2)at2^2; solve for a.

推理：按斜面几何关系，斜面上任一点的竖直下降量与水平位移之比为 tan37°=0.75。

raw_record.original_question:
As shown in the figure, an inclined plane with an angle $\theta=37^{\circ}$ and height $h=1.8\mathrm{m}$ is located on a horizontal ground. A small ball is thrown horizontally to the right from point A at the top of the inclined plane with an initial velocity $v_{0}$, and the ball just lands at point B at the bottom of the inclined plane. Air resistance is negligible, and the gravitational acceleration is taken as $g=10\mathrm{m}/\mathrm{s}^{2}$, with $\tan 37^{\circ}=0.75$.

1. Determine the magnitude of the initial velocity $v_{0}$ of the projectile.
2. If the inclined plane starts to move to the right with a uniformly accelerated linear motion from rest on the horizontal plane at the same time the ball is thrown horizontally, and the ball lands on the inclined plane after $t_{2}=0.3\mathrm{s}$, find the magnitude of the acceleration of the inclined plane.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the attached figure, point A is at the upper-left end of the inclined plane, directly below A is the left-end foot point on the horizontal ground, and the vertical height is labeled h. The small ball is thrown horizontally to the right from point A, and the initial velocity is labeled v0. The inclined plane extends from A downward to the right to point B on the ground, the angle between inclined plane AB and the horizontal ground is labeled 37°, and B is on the ground on the right side.

Reasoning: Take the fixed ground reference frame, set the ground point directly below A as the coordinate origin, the x-axis horizontal to the right, and the y-axis vertical upward, then the coordinate of point A is (0,h), and the coordinate of point B is (L,0). From the right-triangle relationship in the figure, the angle between the inclined plane and the horizontal is 37°, so tan37° = h/L, therefore L = h/tan37° = 1.8/0.75 = 2.4 m.

First question: The small ball is thrown horizontally from point A, and the equations of motion are x = v0 t, y = h - (1/2)gt^2. When the small ball just lands at point B, y=0, so 0 = 1.8 - (1/2)×10×t^2, giving t = sqrt(2h/g) = sqrt(3.6/10) = 0.6 s. At this time x=L=2.4 m, so v0 = L/t = 2.4/0.6 = 4 m/s.

Second question: The inclined plane starts from rest and makes uniformly accelerated linear motion to the right; when t2=0.3 s, the horizontal displacement is s = (1/2)at2^2. After the whole inclined plane moves to the right, its line equation is y = h - tan37°(x - s). The small ball still makes horizontal projectile motion in the ground reference frame; when t2=0.3 s, x = v0 t2 = 4×0.3 = 1.2 m, y = h - (1/2)gt2^2 = 1.8 - 0.5×10×0.3^2 = 1.35 m. Substitute into the moved inclined-plane equation: 1.35 = 1.8 - 0.75(1.2 - s). Simplifying gives 1.35 = 0.9 + 0.75s, so s = 0.6 m. Also s = (1/2)a×0.3^2, therefore a = 2s/t2^2 = 1.2/0.09 = 13.3 m/s^2.
